Maximum Loadability of Islanded Microgrids With
Renewable Energy Generation
Xiaoyuan Xu , Member, IEEE, Zheng Yan , Mohammad Shahidehpour , Fellow, IEEE,
Sijie Chen , Member, IEEE,H a nW a n g ,Z h i y iL i, Member, IEEE,
and Quan Zhou, Graduate Student Member, IEEE
Abstract—A microgrid (MG) is a small-scale power system
which is fed by constrained distributed generation (DG) units
and its continuous operation is affected by the variability of
available generation resources. In this paper, a global sensitivity
analysis (GSA) method is proposed to evaluate the impact of vari-
able energy resources on the maximum loadability of islanded
MGs (IMGs). First, a probabilistic optimization problem is for-
mulated to calculate the IMG load margin considering the droop
characteristics of DG units and uncertainties of renewable gener-
ation, loads and distribution feeder parameters. Next, the global
sensitivity (GS) is introduced that can identify the impact of inde-
pendent and correlated variables on the IMG loadability. Last,
the sparse polynomial chaos expansion method is used to obtain
the probabilistic models for IMG load margins, and an efﬁcient
GSA method is proposed to calculate the GS of IMG loadability
to prevailing variables. The probabilistic models are considered
for IMG input variables and the impact of variable correlations
on IMG loadability is analyzed. The proposed method for cal-
culating the maximum loadability is tested using a 33-bus IMG
and the results are compared with those of other GSA and local
sensitivity analysis methods.
Index Terms—Microgrids, maximum loadability, global sensi-
tivity analysis, polynomial chaos expansion.

I. I NTRODUCTION
M
ICROGRID (MG) is operated either in grid-connected
or islanded mode. In the grid-connected mode, the
frequency and voltages of MGs are determined by the util-
ity grid which is represented as an inﬁnite bus. In islanded
MGs (IMGs), the frequency and voltages are regulated by DG
units governed by the respective droop characteristics. The
IMG operation could enhance the reliability and the resilience
of utility grid when the power system is facing outages. In
the literature, various methods have been proposed for the
planning and operation of IMGs [ 1]–[8].
The maximum loadability of transmisison systems, which
maintains the large-scale voltage stability, was studied exten-
sively. For a distribution system (DS), the related work is quite
limited since the DS loadability was traditionally managed by
the connected main grid. Recently, the maximum IMG load-
ability has attracted additional attention since IMGs are fed
in the island mode by small DG units which could enhance
the loadability of IMG. The existing loadability approach
evaluates the distance from the current operating point to
the critical operating point for maintaining reliable and sta-
ble operations of IMGs. Reference [ 9] studied the maximum
IMG loadability by calculating the equilibrium point using
the Fischer-Burmeister-based method. Reference [ 10] evalu-
ated the maximum loadability of droop-controlled IMGs using
the optimal power ﬂow method in which a complementary
constraint was added to describe the capacity-limited DG unit
operations. Reference [ 11] proposed a probabilistic algorithm
to determine the optimal droop settings of IMGs. The algo-
rithm adopted a hierarchical approach to expand the IMG load
margin while satisfying the prevailing operating constraints.
IMGs can face various uncertainties including load and
renewable energy forecast errors as well as random DS
network outages. Accordingly, probabilistic methods are
applied when evaluating the maximum IMG loadability in
which the scenarios with minor impacts on IMG operations are
disregarded. Therefore, a quick identiﬁcation of critical vari-
ables could accelerate IMG loadability analyses and improve
its controllability.
Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) is an effective method
for quantifying the impact of IMG input variables on the
MG performance [ 12]. Different from local sensitivity anal-
ysis (LSA), GSA considers system nonlinearities and interac-
tions among pertinent variables. By decomposing the output
variance into segments attributed to a subset of inputs, we
deﬁne the ratio of the segment to the total variance as the
global sensitivity (GS) of input variables for evaluating IMG
variables.
GSA was generally applied to artiﬁcial neural network [ 13]
and hydrological modeling [ 14], with a limited applications
to power systems. Recently, [ 15] introduced GSA to evalu-
ate uncertainties in DS operations. Reference [ 16] compared
GSA with LSA for identifying critical uncertainties in small
signal stability analyses. However, GS was mostly calculated
using a crude Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) method, which
required large sample sizes to obtain accurate results, making
GSA a time-consuming and expensive approach for large-
scale problems. In [ 17] and [ 18], an improved GSA method
was proposed to evaluate the impact of input variables on
DS power ﬂows. This method was improved by using sparse
polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) to perform the high-
dimensional model representation (HDMR) decomposition,
thus presenting analytical GS solutions for independent vari-
ables. However, the HDMR decomposition is non-unique for
correlated variables [19]. Besides, the correlation of variables,
which affects the solution for uncertain variables, was not
detailed in previous GSA applications.
In this paper, GSA is applied to IMGs with renewable
energy generation. First, a probabilistic nonlinear optimization
problem is established to calculate the load margin of IMGs
considering DG droop characteristics and variabilities of
renewable energy generation, loads and DS network parame-
ters. Then, GSA is applied to IMG loadability with correlated
input variables using conditional probability and Copula func-
tions. Next, a surrogate model of load margin is established to
calculate GS values, and an efﬁcient GSA method is proposed
to analyze the impact of input variables on the IMG load mar-
gin. The proposed GSA method is tested using a 33-bus IMG
with various types of input variables, and the results are com-
pared with those considering other sensitivity analysis methods
to validate the effectiveness of the proposed GSA method.
II. M
AXIMUM LOADABILITY ASSESSMENT OF IMG
In this section, the models are presented for DG units
and loads. Then, probability models are developed for input
variables. Finally, a probabilistic optimization problem is
established to evaluate the maximum IMG loadability.
A. DG Model
There are three types of power system nodes, including PV ,
PQ and reference nodes, for balancing the total generation
and load. In IMGs, DG units are responsible for regulating
the frequency and voltages while satisfying load sharing. DG
units in IMGs are usually modeled as droop, PV or PQ nodes.
In general, there are three droop control strategies: P-f /Q-
V, P-V/Q-f and generalized droop, with the assumption of
inductive, resistive and complex impedances, respectively. In
this paper, the P-f /Q-V droop is adopted, which decouples
active and reactive power controls and mimics the behavior of
a synchronous generator in power systems. Moreover, a virtual

IV . GSA
FOR MAXIMUM IMG L OADABILITY
MCS is usually used to perform GSA which requires many
samples to obtain accurate results, which limits the practical
GSA applications. In this paper, an efﬁcient GSA method is
proposed to analyze the impacts of variables on the loadabil-
ity of IMGs. Instead of directly calculating GSs with MCS,
a surrogate model for the load margin is ﬁrst established with
PCE, and then GS is calculated using the surrogate model.

V. C ASE STUDIES
In this section, the proposed GSA method is tested using
a 33-bus IMG. The variabilities of loads, feeder parameters
and renewable power are modeled as random variables, and
the correlation of renewable power outputs is considered. The
proposed method is compared with other GSA and LSA meth-
ods for evaluating the impacts of variables. Programs are
developed with MATLAB 8.1 on a PC with Intel Core i7
3.6GHz CPU and 8GB of RAM. Sobol sequences are used to
generate samples of random variables. The OPTI toolbox [ 27]
is used to solve the nonlinear optimization problem (8). The
UQLab toolbox is used to calculate SPCE coefﬁcients.

VI. C
ONCLUSION
In this paper, a GSA method is proposed to evalu-
ate the impact of variables on the maximum IMG load-
ability. Considering MG characteristics operating in the
islanded mode and the probability distribution models of
uncertainties, a probabilistic optimization problem is estab-
lished to evaluate IMG load margins. Then, GSs are
presented to evaluate the importance of independent and
correlated variables. In order to improve the efﬁciency of
GSA, SPCE is used to establish probability models of
load margins, and GSs are calculated based on surrogate
models.
The proposed method is tested using a 33-bus IMG system
which is compared with other SA methods. The simulation
results indicate that SPCE overcomes the PCE deﬁciency
in high-dimensional problems by reducing the number of
polynomial chaos bases, thus much fewer coefﬁcients are
estimated in establishing surrogate models. Compared with
LSs, GSs consider the power system nonlinearity and describe
the impact of variable dependence on the output. GSA-
SPCE obtains accurate GSs and is much more efﬁcient than
GSA-MCS and GSA-PCE. For IMGs with various uncertain-
ties, accurate identiﬁcation of the most inﬂuencing variables
will reduce the number of variables in IMG analyses and
help manage the impact of variabilities with proper control
strategies, such as the installation of energy storage systems.
